extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of Mochizuki's IUT series (specialists in Frobenioids, theta monoids, and Kummer theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Globalize the multiradial portion of local theta-monoid theory to the log-theta-lattice, construct associated Frobenioids and Kummer isomorphisms, and analyse the resulting indeterminacies (Kummer-detachment and étale-transport) for transport between arithmetic holomorphic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertically Coric Theta Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: There are functorial algorithms in the D- and D'‑prime-strips associated to the Θ±ellNF‑Hodge theater for constructing collections of data indexed by V → Ψenv(†D>)v; V → ∞Ψenv(†D>)v as well as a global realiﬁed Frobenioid D_env(†D'>) ∼→ V equipped with a bijection Prime(D_env(†D'>)) and corresponding local isomorphisms for each v ∈ V (cf. [IUTchII], Corollary 4.5, (v)). Each isomorphism induced by a vertical arrow of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induces compatible collections of isomorphisms between the indexed data for adjacent n,m indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the vertical coricity assertion of Proposition 2.1(i); it specifies the functorial construction and compatibility of the data and global realiﬁed Frobenioid with respect to vertical arrows of the log-theta-lattice. The final Frobenioid is compatible with the respective 'Prime(−)' bijections and local isomorphisms for each v.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Isomorphisms (global)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are functorial algorithms in the Θ±ellNF‑Hodge theater for constructing collections of data indexed by V → ΨFenv(†HT Θ)v; V → ∞ΨFenv(†HT Θ)v and a global realiﬁed Frobenioid C_env(†HT Θ) ∼→ V with corresponding local isomorphisms, together with Kummer isomorphisms ΨFenv(†HT Θ) ∼→ Ψenv(†D>); ∞ΨFenv(†HT Θ) ∼→ ∞Ψenv(†D>) and an isomorphism of Frobenioids C_env(†HT Θ) ∼→ D_env(†D'>) compatible with Prime(−) and local isomorphisms (cf. [IUTchII], Corollary 4.6, (iv), (v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kummer isomorphisms tie the Frobenioid-level data arising from Θ‑theory to the D‑side data; the constructions are functorial in the Hodge theater and compatible with the Prime bijections and local isomorphisms. The collection Ψenv(†D>) gives rise to F^(3)- and F^(4)-prime-strips as in [IUTchII], Corollary 4.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Theory at Bad Primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion at v ∈ Vbad of the Kummer isomorphisms is obtained by composing the Kummer isomorphisms of [IUTchII], Proposition 3.3, (i) (defined by forming Kummer classes in mono-theta environments from tempered Frobenioids) with isomorphisms on cohomology classes induced by the full poly-isomorphism of projective systems of mono-theta environments between tempered-Frobenioid-derived and tempered-fundamental-group-derived systems. In particular, the composite map Π_μ(MΘ_*(†D>,v)) ⊗ Q/Z → (Ψ^†F Θ_v)^×μ obtained via these maps is equal to the zero map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a precise technical vanishing statement at bad primes: the composite from exterior cyclotomes (after tensoring with Q/Z) into the target μ‑part of the Ψ†F Θ_v units is zero. The construction uses the full poly-isomorphism and the induced isomorphisms on exterior cyclotomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Theory at Good Nonarchimedean Primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit portion at v ∈ Vgood ⊆ Vnon of the Kummer isomorphisms is obtained as the unit portion of a labeled version of the isomorphism of ind-topological monoids equipped with a topological group action (an 'MLF-Galois TM-pair') discussed in [IUTchII], Proposition 4.2, (i), and may be seen as the labeled version of the 'Kummer poly-isomorphism of semi-simpliﬁcations' in [IUTchII], Proposition 4.2, (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At good nonarchimedean primes the Kummer identifications are realized via labeled versions of the semi-simplified Kummer poly-isomorphism; the statement emphasizes compatibility with the Aut_F(†F^(4)_env)-orbit of the isomorphisms and references labeled constructions in [IUTchII].

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Theory at Archimedean Primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit portion at v ∈ Varc of the Kummer isomorphisms is obtained as the unit portion of a labeled version of the isomorphism of topological monoids discussed in [IUTchII], Proposition 4.4, (i). The portion at v ∈ Varc of the AutF(†F^(4)_env)-orbit of the second isomorphism may be obtained as a labeled version of the 'Kummer poly-isomorphism of semi-simpliﬁcations' given in [IUTchII], Proposition 4.4, (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archimedean primes require treating the topological monoid isomorphisms and their labeled versions; the text points to the analogous semi-simplification description in [IUTchII].

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Constant Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of the unit portion of the theta monoids gives rise to natural isomorphisms †F^(3)×_env ∼→ †F^(3)×_env; F^(3)×(†D^(3)_env) ∼→ F^(3)×_env(†D>) of the respective associated F^(3)×-prime-strips; these natural isomorphisms are compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms and Theorem 1.5, (iii) (cf. [IUTchII], Corollary 4.10, (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility ties the unit/constant portions of the theta monoids to the constant monoids (F^(3)× etc.) and ensures coherence with the Kummer identifications and previously established results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step strategy for describing objects across arithmetic holomorphic structures
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe an object constructed in one arithmetic holomorphic structure from the point of view of a distinct arithmetic holomorphic structure, break the operation into two steps: (a) passing from Frobenius-like structures to étale-like structures via various Kummer isomorphisms; (b) transporting the resulting étale-like structures from one arithmetic holomorphic structure to another by means of various multiradiality properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that both steps are necessary: (a) converts Frobenius-like (mono-theta / Frobenioid) data into étale-like data using Kummer theory; (b) uses multiradial transport (e.g., bi-coricity/multiradiality) to move that data between vertical lines. The computation of what the object 'looks like' on the other side reduces to computing the indeterminacies arising in (a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer-detachment indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminacies that arise from step (a): the passage from Frobenius-like structures to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms. These are referred to as Kummer-detachment indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include the non-commutativity of certain Frobenius-picture diagrams (choice of path from a '•' to a coric '◦') where 'upper semi-commutativity' gives an upper estimate of the indeterminacy; also (ℤ̂)×-indeterminacies discussed in Remark 1.4.2 and the final Kummer isomorphism display of Theorem 1.5, (iii). The theory of mono-theta environments (rigidity properties) is used to ensure these indeterminacies are sufficiently mild to enable reconstruction algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-transport indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminacies that occur as a result of executing various 'anabelian' or 'group-theoretic' algorithms when transporting étale-like structures between arithmetic holomorphic structures (step (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fundamental example is the indeterminacy coming from automorphisms of local absolute Galois groups G_v for v ∈ Vnon that are not of scheme-theoretic origin; such automorphisms create étale-transport ambiguities in Theorem 1.5, (iii),(iv). The text treats these as distinct from Kummer-detachment indeterminacies and analyses them via reconstruction algorithms and multiradiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment: cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic rigidity: a specific isomorphism between the interior and exterior cyclotomes arising from a mono-theta environment, a consequence of the nondegenerate (quadratic) nature of the commutator '[−,−]' of the theta groups (the degree of the commutator is precisely 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclotomic rigidity can be viewed as a rigidification of a projective line of cyclotomes and is fundamentally nonlinear. Composing it with an N-th power morphism sacrifices constant multiple rigidity; the distinguished nature of the 'first power' is important. The multiradiality of mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity stands in contrast to classical MLF‑Galois pair cyclotomic rigidity and plays a central role in §2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment: discrete rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete rigidity: a property arising from the degree of the commutator being ≤ 2, which assures one can restrict attention to Z‑multiples/powers (as opposed to ℤ̂‑multiples/powers) of divisors, line bundles, and rational functions on tempered coverings of a Tate curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrete rigidity prevents the need for a ℤ̂‑theory of divisors/line bundles/rational functions (which would blur positivity notions). It ensures one can work with integral multiples and maintain conventional isomorphism structures between line bundles, which is critical for the Frobenioid-theoretic mono-theta constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment: constant multiple rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant multiple rigidity: rigidity that plays a role in constructing canonical splittings of theta monoids via restriction to the zero section (cf. [IUTchII], Corollary 1.12, (ii); Proposition 3.3, (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constant multiple rigidity ensures uniqueness properties (up to constants) necessary for canonical splittings and for maintaining control when considering powers / multiples in Kummer towers. Loss of this rigidity can occur when composing cyclotomic rigidity with N-th power morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment: isomorphism class compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Isomorphism class compatibility: the convention that various objects of the tempered Frobenioids and their base categories are known only up to isomorphism (compatibility with the topology of the tempered fundamental group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is essential because objects in Kummer towers correspond to single fields/rings (not just multiplicative groups), and reconstruction algorithms must respect that objects are only determined up to indeterminate isomorphisms. It underlies the algorithmic treatment of non-isomorphic line bundles arising from N-th root extractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment: Frobenioid structure compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility with the Frobenioid structure: compatibility of the mono-theta environment with the Frobenioid's monoidal portion equipped with its natural Galois action (i.e., compatibility with 'Frobenius-like' monoidal structures used to perform constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility is crucial because the Frobenius-like monoidal portion is used (via Kummer theory) to relate non-scheme-theoretic constructions (log-, Θ-, Θ×μ-, Θ×μ_gau-links) to étale-like structures; it ensures the monoidal/Galois actions are coherent with mono-theta rigidity properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation discrete rigidity (complements on tempered coverings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A form of discrete rigidity concerned with evaluation points: the 'global bookkeeping operations' on labels of evaluation points force restrictions to 'complements on tempered coverings' so that one may restrict attention to discrete Z‑conjugates (rather than profinite ℤ̂‑conjugates) of theta functions; this is referred to as 'evaluation discrete rigidity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion addresses whether evaluation-point coordinates lie in Z or in ℤ̂ and whether one can use a partially tempered fundamental group Π^† instead of the full tempered fundamental group Π for certain constructions. The discussion notes these evaluation-related issues will be relevant in §3, and that Π^† = ℤ̂×(⋯) considerations affect whether discrete rigidity suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequacy of replacing conjugate synchronization by diagonal conjugacy identification (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: A naive approach to avoid conjugate synchronization is to work with the (G×...×G)-conjugacy class of the diagonal embedding G → G×...×G, identifying (g,g) with its (G×G)-conjugates; however, identifying elements that differ by factors like (1,[h,g]) is incompatible with the convention that such factors correspond to distinct elements at distinct components and is therefore inadequate because of the highly nonabelian nature of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a negative principle: one must not collapse distinct components by identifying conjugates of the diagonal if one needs to keep distinct Galois-theoretic Kummer classes (theta values) at distinct components. The incompatibility is an essential reason the simpler apparatus fails for the series of papers' purposes.
